actually_viewed.caption: University caption dates photograph to 1884; reproduced in American Cattle Producer, July 1947, Benjamin F. Davis papers, Box 9, UW American Heritage Center.
observed: Long elevated porch across front and around right side, broad front steps and narrower side steps.
Single main wall storey below a steep mansard roof with four front dormers; a taller central square tower has paired narrow windows and its own mansard cap with a front dormer.
Bracketed eaves, tall chimneys, sash windows and diagonal braces at porch posts.
Unpaved foreground; rocking chairs present but not yet a proposed model feature.
limits: Monochrome print reproduction does not establish colours, exact materials, dimensions, rear elevation or detailed joinery.
Do not infer a roof material solely from the dark printed tone.
No people to copy or invent.

sources_read.supports: Cattlemen founded a social club in 1880 with dining, reading, billiard and lodging spaces; establishes institution and function.
Wyoming cattle-boom context and club mansard roof.
Period Second Empire forms: mansard, dormers, brackets, tower and porch.
Late nineteenth-century slate distribution, roofs with staggered joints, patterned/coloured slates suitable for Second Empire mansards. Natural slate colours include blue-grey, green, purple and red.
sources_read.limits: Period material/type analogue; not proof of Cheyenne Club’s exact covering or colours.

sources_read.actual_document: Downtown Cheyenne Historic District, boundary increase III, 1996 nomination with 2018 additional documentation. Filename 2021 reflects a search result, not authorship date.
sources_read.supports: Club construction in 1881, mansard roof and two full-length verandas. Idelman Block (1884) documents local red brick with pale mineral insets.
sources_read.limits: Idelman masonry is a regional material analogue only. The later 1982 Cheyenne Club entry is excluded.

sources_read.supports: Traditional white-pigment paint and oil paint used on wood trim; warm-white trim is a period palette reconstruction.
sources_read.limits: General material availability, not proof of the original club’s paint.

date_uncertainty: 1880 institution founding and 1881 clubhouse construction are distinguished; the 1884 photograph establishes visible form. Earlier source summaries that collapse these dates are not used for exact construction chronology.

material_decision: Fictional red-brick clubhouse with warm-white timber trim and natural blue-grey/purple slate mansards. Regional brick and general period slate/paint evidence support availability, not an exact Cheyenne Club palette.
